about: spec-v1974: per-state adoption of the IFGC, drafted one state at a time from the state's own statute or rule, with ICC's adoption map as the cross-check only. Each row also names its code family (a state on the UPC or UMC adopts no IPC or IMC edition). All 51 drafted 2026-10-20 from the state's own rule where found, ICC's April 2026 adoption chart as the cross-check; unsigned rows show labeled not verified, and a row whose sources conflict shows no edition.

AL.name: Alabama
AL.scope: Minimum standard for certified gas fitters where no local code is adopted; DCM also adopts the 2021 IFGC for state-funded work and schools.
AL.citation: Ala. Admin. Code r. 720-X-1-.02(1)(c) (2021 IFGC for commercial gas), Plumbers and Gas Fitters Examining Board
AL.draft_note: Read rule 720-X-1-.02 PDF: certified gas contractors 'shall comply with the minimum standards of the 2021 International Fuel Gas Code for commercial gas installations'; applies 'In the absence of locally adopted codes'; eff 2022-10-15. DCM rule 355-12-1-.01(1)(d) also adopts the 2021 IFGC for its building scope. HVAC Board rule 440-X-5 cites the IFGC with no edition. Signer: statewide vs limited is a judgment call.

AK.name: Alaska
AK.pending: DPS review of the 2024 IFGC (with IBC/IFC/IMC) underway; public notice estimated summer 2026, none found.
AK.scope: Gas piping under UPC 2018 ch. 12 (8 AAC 63.010). 2021 IFGC adopted only for s. 304 and ch. 6-7 (appliances, hydrogen), 13 AAC 50.024.
AK.citation: 8 AAC 63.010 (UPC 2018, incl. ch. 12 fuel gas); 13 AAC 50.024 (2021 IFGC s. 304, ch. 6-7 only)
AK.draft_note: Read 13 AAC 50.024: 'The International Fuel Gas Code 2021 Edition (IFGC), Chapter 3 Section 304 and Chapters 6 and 7, are adopted' for fuel gas utilization equipment and gaseous hydrogen; 13 AAC 50.023 replaces IFGC references with 'Plumbing Code as adopted by 8 AAC 63.010'. Read 8 AAC 63.010: UPC 2018 chapters 2-17 incl. ch. 12 with an Alaska LP-gas amendment to 1210.2.3. So gas piping sizing follows the UPC; family recorded as UPC. Signer: alternative is family IFGC, status limited, 2021 (eff ~2022-10-28) for the partial adoption.

AZ.name: Arizona
AZ.scope: No statewide IFGC; cities and counties adopt their own plumbing/mechanical/gas codes.
AZ.citation: No state adoption: counties adopt building codes under A.R.S. 11-861; cities by reference under A.R.S. 9-802
AZ.draft_note: An absence has no adopting rule to cite. A.R.S. 11-861 and 9-802 (read for the IBC row) give counties and cities code-adoption authority; no state IFGC adoption found (ROC licenses contractors but adopts no installation code). citation_primary true because the statutes show local authority; signer may prefer false. Local editions not checked.
AZ.icc_2026_10_20: Chart: IFGC X. State page: codes are adopted locally.

AR.name: Arkansas
AR.citation: Ark. Code R. 007.24.20-002 (2018 Arkansas Fuel Gas Code, based on 2018 IFGC), Dept. of Health, Plumbing and Natural Gas
AR.draft_note: Read the LII record for rule 007.24.20-002 '2018 Arkansas Fuel Gas Code': adopted by Arkansas Register Vol. MMXXI No. 08, eff. 8/12/2021 (full text not on LII). 2018 IFGC base from ICC's state page and ICC product listing, not the rule text. No newer edition found.
AR.icc_2026_10_20: Chart: IFGC 18. State page: 2018 AR Fuel Gas Code based on the 2018 IFGC.

CA.name: California
CA.scope: Fuel gas piping is in the California Plumbing Code (2024 UPC ch. 12), effective 2026-01-01; the IFGC is not adopted.
CA.citation: Cal. Code Regs. tit. 24, pt. 5 (2025 California Plumbing Code, ch. 12 Fuel Gas Piping), Building Standards Commission
CA.draft_note: Read BSC codes page and Part 5 ISOR (2024 UPC basis, eff 2026-01-01). No IFGC adoption in Title 24. That ch. 12 of the CPC carries the fuel gas provisions is from the UPC structure, not a line read in the BSC documents; signer confirm.

CO.name: Colorado
CO.scope: Colorado Fuel Gas Code covers fuel gas piping throughout Colorado; IFGC ss. 412-413 excluded.
CO.citation: 3 CCR 720-1, rule 1.2.B (Colorado Fuel Gas Code: 2024 IFGC as amended), State Plumbing Board
CO.draft_note: Read current 3 CCR 720-1 PDF (eff 08/14/2026): rule 1.2.B adopts 'Chapters 2-8 save and except Sections 412 and 413, Appendices A-C of the IFGC, 2024 edition' as the Colorado Fuel Gas Code, governing fuel gas piping 'throughout Colorado'. Prior version (eff 02/14/2026) adopted the IFGC 2021. 2021 start 2023-04-14 from editor's notes; signer confirm. ICC chart lag (April 2026 chart says 21).

CT.name: Connecticut
CT.pending: Draft 2026 CSBC keeps the IFGC unadopted and lists NFPA 54-2024; awaits LRRC approval.
CT.scope: IFGC not adopted; fuel gas follows NFPA 54 (2021 ed.) via the 2022 State Fire Safety Code, effective 2022-10-01.
CT.citation: 2022 CT State Fire Safety Code s. 102.14 and ref. std. NFPA 54-21; CSBC 101.4.1: IFGC not adopted
CT.draft_note: Read the second-resubmitted proposed 2022 CT State Fire Safety Code (CGA LRRC file): '(Add) 102.14 Gas. The International Fuel Gas Code is not adopted by this code' and references go to 'NFPA 54, National Fuel Gas Code'; referenced standards list '54-21: National Fuel Gas Code'. That is the LRRC submission, not the final published code, so citation_primary false. Read the draft 2026 CSBC (Dec 2025): '101.4.1 Gas. The International Fuel Gas Code is not adopted by the state of Connecticut' and lists '54-24 National Fuel Gas Code'. DAS regulations page lists no fuel gas code. Effective date 2022-10-01 with the 2022 codes.

DE.name: Delaware
DE.scope: No statewide fuel gas code found; counties and municipalities adopt their own.
DE.citation: No state adoption: 16 Del. C. 7601 lets the three counties adopt and enforce building codes
DE.draft_note: An absence has no adopting rule to cite. No state IFGC or NFPA 54 adoption found; the state plumbing code (4455) adopts the IPC only. Delaware State Fire Prevention Regulations may reference NFPA 54 for some work (not checked). Counties' fuel gas codes not checked.

FL.name: Florida
FL.pending: 9th Edition (2026) Florida Building Code proposed 2026-09-23 (comment period closed 2026-10-14); no final notice or date yet.
FL.citation: Fla. Admin. Code r. 61G20-1.001 (Florida Building Code, 8th Edition (2023), Fuel Gas), Florida Building Commission
FL.draft_note: Read rule 61G20-1.001 text (flrules .doc, eff 3-18-26): 'The Florida Building Code, 8th Edition (2023), as updated ... is hereby adopted as the building code for the State of Florida'; history includes 12-31-23 (8th Edition). The rule adopts the FBC as a whole; the Fuel Gas volume and its 2021 IFGC base are from ICC/secondary sources, not the rule text. 9th Edition proposed 2026-09-23, pending; ICC/Miami-Dade say effective 2026-12-31. Recheck Dec 2026.

GA.name: Georgia
GA.scope: Mandatory state minimum code; local governments choose whether to enforce, and local amendments must be filed with DCA.
GA.citation: O.C.G.A. 8-2-23; DCA State Minimum Standard Codes: 2024 IFGC with Georgia Amendments
GA.draft_note: Read DCA memo dated 2025-12-01: the DCA Board 'voted to adopt the following codes with an effective date of January 1, 2026', including the '2024 International Fuel Gas Code with Georgia Amendments', as mandatory state codes under O.C.G.A. 8-2-23. Prior edition not recorded.

HI.name: Hawaii
HI.pending: SBCC code-update work suspended under the Governor's housing proclamation; no newer UPC adoption found.
HI.scope: Fuel gas piping under the Hawaii State Plumbing Code (UPC 2018 ch. 12), eff 2020-05-19; the IFGC is not adopted.
HI.citation: Haw. Admin. R. tit. 3, State Building Code Council, State Plumbing Code (UPC 2018) [Eff 5/19/2020]; HRS 107-25
HI.draft_note: Read HAR tit. 3 State Plumbing Code (LII): 'The "Uniform Plumbing Code, 2018 Edition" including appendices ... is incorporated by reference' [Eff 5/19/2020]; scope section applies to all new construction [Eff 5/19/2020]. Read HRS 107-25: state codes are based on the UPC; counties must adopt within 2 years or the state code becomes the county's interim code (Garden Island: counties by 2022-05-19). Uncertain: whether HRS 107's default rule has made a newer UPC the state code (as the SBCC report says for the 2021 IBC/IRC/IECC); SBCC work is suspended under the housing proclamation. County ordinances not checked. No IFGC or NFPA 54 adoption found; gas is assumed to fall under UPC ch. 12, which the adoption section incorporates ('all parts of the Uniform Plumbing Code subject to the amendments'); whether a Hawaii amendment deletes ch. 12 was not checked.

ID.name: Idaho
ID.scope: Applied by the Division statewide; cities/counties running a mechanical permit program must adopt the same codes (Idaho Code 54-5001).
ID.citation: IDAPA 24.39.70.600.02 (Idaho HVAC Board; International Fuel Gas Code, 2018 Edition, appendices A-D, amended)
ID.draft_note: Read the current IDAPA 24.39.70 PDF (created 2026-06-12): rule 600.02 adopts the 2018 IFGC with appendices A-D and Idaho amendments (deletes 109; 406.4 test pressures/duration; 503.4.1.2 plastic vent test; 505.1.1), stamped (3-28-23). Statute and effective-date basis as in the IMC row: 2021-01-01 is secondary (DBS 2018-codes notice). DOPL's 2025 adopted-codes sheet lists the 2018 IFGC.

IL.name: Illinois
IL.scope: No statewide fuel gas code; cities and counties adopt their own (IFGC or NFPA 54).
IL.citation: No state adoption found: Illinois has no statewide fuel gas code; municipalities and counties adopt their own
IL.draft_note: An absence has no adopting rule to cite. Same basis as the IMC row: the non-building-code-jurisdiction inspection list (P.A. 103-510, per the IBC draft) names no fuel gas code. Not checked: State Fire Marshal LP-gas rules (41 Ill. Adm. Code 200, NFPA 58), which cover LP-gas storage, not building fuel gas piping. ICC chart shows X.

IN.name: Indiana
IN.citation: 675 IAC 25-3 (2014 Indiana Fuel Gas Code, based on the 2012 IFGC, Second Printing)
IN.draft_note: Read the IDHS FPBSC rules page: 675 IAC 25-3, 2014 Indiana Fuel Gas Code, 'International Fuel Gas Code, 2012 Edition, Second Printing', effective 12/1/2014, currently in effect. No fuel gas draft listed. IAC text not read.

IA.name: Iowa
IA.scope: Fuel gas piping: UPC 2024 ch. 12 (eff. 2025-03-26); LP-gas: NFPA 54 and 58, 2024 eds. (661 IAC ch. 226, eff. 2025-03-26). IFGC not used.
IA.citation: 481 IAC 425.3(105) (fuel gas piping per UPC 2024 ch. 12, unless in conflict with 661 IAC ch. 226)
IA.draft_note: Read 481 IAC 425.3: fuel gas piping shall comply with UPC 2024 ch. 12 unless it conflicts with 661-ch. 226, which then governs [ARC 8913C, eff. 3/26/25]; 481 IAC 426.3(1) strikes the IMC's IFGC reference for NFPA 54 and NFPA 58 'current edition', 661-226 and the state plumbing code. Read the rules.iowa.gov notice for ARC 8910C: 661 ch. 226 adopts NFPA 54 and NFPA 58, 2024 editions, for LP-gas, effective 2025-03-26. Family 'UPC' because the general piping rule is the UPC's gas chapter; signer may prefer 'NFPA 54'. Note 661 rules may have moved to 481 (IBC row says 11/26/25); 425.3 still cites 661.
IA.icc_2026_10_20: IFGC X (some adoptions; not the statewide standard).

KS.name: Kansas
KS.scope: No statewide fuel gas code; cities and counties adopt their own.
KS.citation: No state adoption found: Kansas has no statewide fuel gas code; cities and counties adopt under home rule
KS.draft_note: An absence has no adopting rule to cite. ICC's April 2026 chart shows X (local adoptions only) for every Kansas I-code; the IBC/IRC rows found no statewide building code (home rule). I found no Kansas statute or K.A.R. adopting a statewide fuel gas code (State Fire Marshal LP-gas rules not checked); did not search exhaustively. Signer: confirm.

KY.name: Kentucky
KY.scope: NFPA 54 National Fuel Gas Code, 2012 edition, as listed by DHBC with the 2018 KBC. Effective date not found.
KY.citation: DHBC list of codes adopted by Kentucky: 2012 NFPA 54 (via 815 KAR 7:120, 2018 Kentucky Building Code)
KY.draft_note: Read DHBC 'Codes Currently Adopted by Kentucky': lists '2012 NFPA 54 - National Fuel Gas Code'; no IFGC. I did not read the KBC amendment document or 815 KAR 20 to see where NFPA 54 is incorporated (KBC ch. 35 or the plumbing code's gas piping rules), so citation_primary false and no effective date. ICC chart IFGC blank agrees.

LA.name: Louisiana
LA.pending: 2024 IFGC proposed (notice of intent, La. Register 2026-08-20); proposed effective 2027-01-01. Final rule not seen.
LA.citation: LAC 17:I (Louisiana State Uniform Construction Code; International Fuel Gas Code 2021, amended)
LA.draft_note: Read the LUCCC code information sheet (revised 2026-08-06): current IFGC edition 2021; '2021 ICC Codes' effective January 1, 2023; next cycle '2024 editions for ICC Codes', 'will become effective January 1, 2027'. The 2024 adoption was still a proposed rule (notice of intent, La. Register 2026-08-20, per the IBC/IRC rows), so it is 'pending', not 'upcoming'. I did not re-read the LAC 17:I section text for this code. Signer: check the Oct/Nov 2026 Register for a final rule.

ME.name: Maine
ME.pending: Fuel Board 2026-27 regulatory agenda lists NFPA 58 updates (search snippet); no NFPA 54 change seen.
ME.scope: NFPA 54 National Fuel Gas Code, 2021 edition, with Fuel Board exclusions/amendments (02-658 C.M.R. ch. 6). Maine adoption date not found.
ME.citation: 02-658 C.M.R. ch. 6, sec. 1 (Maine Fuel Board adopted standards: NFPA 54/ANSI Z223.1, 2021 edition, amended)
ME.draft_note: Read 02-658 ch. 6 sec. 1 on Cornell LII: adopts NFPA 54/ANSI Z223.1 2021 edition ('issued March 15, 2020, effective April 4, 2020' = NFPA's own dates, not Maine's) subject to sec. 6.2.3, plus NFPA 58 2020 and others. A 2024 Board proposal calls the 2021 NFPA 54 'recently adopted'; Maine's adoption effective date not found. citation_primary false (LII copy only; maine.gov 403). IFGC is not used.

MD.name: Maryland
MD.scope: Board also incorporates NFPA 54 and NFPA 58 (most recent versions). WSSC and some counties adopt their own fuel gas codes.
MD.citation: COMAR 09.20.01.01B(3)-(5) (Board adopts the most recent IFGC, NFPA 54 and NFPA 58)
MD.draft_note: Read COMAR 09.20.01.01B: incorporates the most recent version of the IFGC (3), NFPA 54 (4) and NFPA 58 (5); .04 (NFPA 54 modifications) repealed eff. 2025-11-24. Edition 2024 / 2025-11-24 INFERRED as in the IPC row (rule names no year; 2018 IFGC took effect 2019-12-30 per ICC). Family IFGC because the IFGC is listed first and ICC reports the Board 'adopts the IPC and IFGC'; NFPA 54 is also incorporated, so which governs a given installation is unclear.

MA.name: Massachusetts
MA.pending: Board's Gas Code Review sub-committee is reviewing NFPA 54-2024 with modifications (agenda 2025-05-21); no rule seen.
MA.scope: NFPA 54 2012 edition as modified by 248 CMR 5.00 (Massachusetts Fuel Gas Code, 248 CMR 4.00, eff. 2021-04-30).
MA.citation: 248 CMR 4.02-4.03 (Massachusetts Fuel Gas Code: Board adopts NFPA 54, 2012 Edition, as modified by 248 CMR 5.00)
MA.draft_note: Read 248 CMR 4.00 'effective 4/30/21' (mass.gov PDF via Wayback): 4.02 defines NFPA 54 as 'The 2012 Edition of the National Fuel Gas Code'; 4.03(1) adopts NFPA 54 as modified by 248 CMR 5.00 for most gas piping; LP-gas via NFPA 58 2011 and 248 CMR 8.00. Cornell LII shows the same 2012 definition (amended eff. 12/5/2014 and 4/30/2021). Read the Board Gas Code Review agenda 2025-05-21: 'Review Gas Code Changes NFPA-54-24'. The NFPA 54 2012 base appears to date from the 2014-12-05 amendment; 2021-04-30 is the latest 4.00 revision.

MI.name: Michigan
MI.citation: Mich. Admin. Code R 408.30457 (MBC 2801.1: IFGC as listed in MBC ch. 35); 2021 Michigan Building Code
MI.draft_note: SOURCES CONFLICT: ICC's April 2026 chart says IFGC 15. No Michigan rule names an IFGC edition directly: R 408.30457 (Cornell copy) requires mechanical systems to meet the Michigan Mechanical Code 'and the international fuel gas code listed in chapter 35'; the 2021 MBC (effective 2025-04-09) and 2021 MMC (effective 2024-03-12) chapter 35 lists point to the 2021 IFGC (inferred from the 2021 I-code reference lists, not read in the Michigan books). Troy lists '2021 International Fuel Gas Code, IFGC 2015' (ambiguous); Ann Arbor lists 2021 IFGC. Edition and date are inferences; signer may prefer no edition.

MN.name: Minnesota
MN.pending: DLI chapter 1346 docket: request for comments 2026-02-02 on the 2024 IMC and IFGC; draft, hearing and dates 'to be determined'.
MN.citation: Minn. R. 1346.5050 (Minnesota Fuel Gas Code: 2018 IFGC chapters 2-8, as amended)
MN.draft_note: 1346.5050 read 2026-10-20: chapters 2 to 8 of the 2018 IFGC incorporated (history ends 44 SR 1085). Revisor rule record R-04515 read: effective April 06, 2020 (same rule as the mechanical code). Same metro/opt-in enforcement caveat as the IBC row.

MS.name: Mississippi
MS.scope: Council codes are minimum codes localities may adopt (coastal counties must enforce); edition not confirmed.
MS.citation: Miss. Code Ann. 17-2-1 et seq. (Mississippi Building Codes Council), not read directly
MS.draft_note: SOURCES CONFLICT: ICC's April 2026 chart (column read by position) lists IFGC 18; ICC's state page says the Council adopted the 2018 I-codes incl. IFGC in December 2019; an ICC-NTA post (2026-07-20, via search) says the 2024 I-codes incl. IFGC apply to modular construction from 2026-07-01. The Council's adopted-codes list and 17-2-1 text were not reached. Localities adopt one of the last three editions or opted out; coastal counties must enforce. Kept 'local' with no edition, as the IBC and IRC rows are.
MS.icc_2026_10_20: Chart (April 2026): IFGC 18 (state). State page: MBCC 3-year cycle; voluntary outside coastal counties.

MO.name: Missouri
MO.scope: No statewide code; cities and counties adopt their own code and edition.
MO.citation: No state adoption: Missouri has no statewide fuel gas code; counties and cities adopt codes by ordinance
MO.draft_note: An absence has no adopting rule to cite; no Missouri statute was read. ICC's chart marks every I-code X (local only); its state page says the state adopts codes only for state-owned buildings (edition not found, as in the IBC row).

MT.name: Montana
MT.citation: ARM Title 24, Ch. 301 (IFGC 2024 as amended), per DLI Current Codes
MT.draft_note: DLI Current Codes page read 2026-10-20: 'International Fuel Gas Code, 2024 Edition - Effective: September 26, 2026', amended by ARM Title 24 Ch. 301 (specific rule number not read). Prior: 2021 IFGC, believed effective 2022-06-11 (date carried from the IBC/IRC rows, not re-read). Certified local programs enforce the state code; the state enforces elsewhere.

NE.name: Nebraska
NE.scope: No statewide fuel gas code; localities adopt their own. State fire code once listed NFPA 54-2002 (currency unknown).
NE.citation: No state adoption: Neb. Rev. Stat. 71-6403 (state building code) names no fuel gas code; localities adopt their own
NE.draft_note: 71-6403 read 2026-10-20: no fuel gas code in the state building code. A State Fire Marshal Title 153 ch. 1 PDF (updated 2004) lists NFPA 54-2002 in the state fire code; whether a newer fire code edition replaced it was not found, so no NFPA 54 row is drafted. ICC's X marks local adoptions.

NV.name: Nevada
NV.scope: State buildings: fuel gas under the 2024 UPC/UMC (SPWD); other buildings: local codes.
NV.citation: NAC 341.045 (State Public Works Board: UPC/UMC for state buildings), as amended by R072-24A
NV.draft_note: SPWD Adopted Codes list (rev. 2024-02-13, under NAC 341.045) read: '2024 Uniform Plumbing Code (UPC)' and '2024 Uniform Mechanical Code (UMC)'; 2018-edition designs accepted until 2025-06-30. The leg.state.nv.us NAC 341.045 text (stale, 2018 IBC) replaces IPC/IMC references with UPC/UMC. Effective 2024-11-15 per the IBC row's Cornell reading of R072-24A (not re-read). Private buildings: local codes only (southern Nevada jurisdictions phasing in the 2024 UPC/UMC). The SPWD list names no fuel gas code; fuel gas piping falls to the UPC (ch. 12) and UMC, an inference. ICC's X is local IFGC use.

NH.name: New Hampshire
NH.scope: NFPA 54 via the state fire code: 2021 per the 2024 state list; likely 2024 since NFPA 1-2024 took effect 2026-07-27 (unconfirmed).
NH.citation: RSA 153:1, VI-a (state fire code: NFPA 1 and NFPA 101, 2024, incl. referenced codes such as NFPA 54); Saf-FMO 300
NH.draft_note: RSA 153:1 VI-a read 2026-10-20: state fire code is NFPA 101 and NFPA 1, 2024 editions, and includes codes they reference (last change 2026 ch. 104:1, eff. July 27, 2026). The state building code (RSA 155-A:1 IV) names no fuel gas code. State adopted-codes list of 2024-08-13 (via town copies, search) listed '2021 NFPA 54 ... as amended by Saf-FMO 300'. Whether NFPA 54-2024 now applies via NFPA 1-2024 was not confirmed.

NJ.name: New Jersey
NJ.citation: N.J.A.C. 5:23-3.22 (fuel gas subcode: IFGC/2024, New Jersey edition), R.2026 d.086
NJ.draft_note: Adoption notice 58 N.J.R. 8(2) (R.2026 d.086) read: amends N.J.A.C. 5:23-3.14 to 3.22, adopted 2026-07-15, effective August 17, 2026. The notice's rule text shows only changed paragraphs, so the fuel gas subcode edition line was not seen; a DCA Code Advisory Board agenda (2024-08-09, via search) names IFGC/2024 under 5:23-3.22. Six-month grace period (N.J.A.C. 5:23-1.6, not read): prior IFGC/2021 usable until about 2027-02-17. Prior IFGC/2021 effective date not read (IRC row gives 2022-09-06 for the 2021 cycle). The UCC is uniform statewide.

NM.name: New Mexico
NM.scope: Fuel gas piping under UPC 2021 chapter 12 (2021 New Mexico Plumbing Code), effective 2022-03-10.
NM.citation: 14.8.2.22 NMAC (2021 NM Plumbing Code: UPC chapter 12, Fuel Piping, as amended)
NM.draft_note: 14.8.2.22 read: 'CHAPTER 12 FUEL PIPING: See this chapter of the UPC except as provided below' (NM amendments follow). Fuel gas piping is under the 2021 UPC as adopted by 14.8.2 NMAC; LP-gas has its own rules (not read). ICC's X is local IFGC use.

NY.name: New York
NY.scope: Statewide outside New York City, which enforces its own NYC Construction Codes.
NY.citation: 19 NYCRR Part 1224 (2025 Fuel Gas Code of New York State, Uniform Code)
NY.draft_note: Read DOS 19 NYCRR Part 1224 PDF (dos.ny.gov/19-nycrr-part-1224): 1224.2(a) requires compliance with the 2025 FGCNYS, incorporated by reference, published by ICC; Part 1219 lists Parts 1220-1229. DOS notice of adoption: 2025 Uniform Code (incl. 2025 FGCNYS, publication July 2025) effective 2025-12-31; 2020 or 2025 optional during transition. Base edition 2024 IFGC per DOS Code Outreach 2026-1 ('based on the 2024 ICC books with NY modifications', read for the IBC row); the Part 1224 PDF itself does not name the IFGC year. Prior: 2020 FGCNYS (2018 IFGC). NYC excluded.

NC.name: North Carolina
NC.pending: 2024 NC Fuel Gas Code (2021 IFGC) adopted; effective 12 months after OSFM certification under S.L. 2025-2; not yet certified.
NC.citation: N.C.G.S. 143-138; 2018 North Carolina State Building Code: Fuel Gas Code (Office of State Fire Marshal)
NC.draft_note: SOURCES CONFLICT: ICC Apr 2026 chart shows IFGC 21, but the 2024 NC codes are not yet effective. OSFM Codes Current and Past (read): 2018 NC Fuel Gas Code effective 2019-01-01 and 'currently effective', with the 2018 NC amendments 'along with the 2015 International Codes'. The 2024 section of that page covers only the Building Code; the S.L. 2025-2 sec. 5.12(b) delay (all ten 2024 codes effective 12 months after the State Fire Marshal's certification) is from the OSFM 2025-03-31 letter read for the IBC row. No certification found as of 2026-10-20. 2024 NC base = 2021 IFGC per ICC chart (OSFM page does not name it).
NC.icc_2026_10_20: ICC chart (Apr 2026): IFGC 21 (counts the adopted, not-yet-effective 2024 NC code)

ND.name: North Dakota
ND.scope: Applies only where a city, county or township elects to enforce a building code; the state does not enforce it.
ND.citation: N.D.C.C. ch. 54-21.3 (North Dakota State Building Code), Dept. of Commerce, Division of Community Services
ND.draft_note: Commerce page (read): on 2025-09-11 eligible cities, counties and BCAC members adopted the 2024 IBC, IRC, IMC and IFGC; new State Building Code effective 2026-01-01; Community Services 'not involved in the enforcement'; adopting localities must enforce it and may amend. NDCC 54-21.3-03 (read for the IBC row) requires the code to consist of the international building, residential, mechanical and fuel gas codes. NDAC rule text adopting the 2024 IFGC not read.

OH.name: Ohio
OH.scope: No separate Ohio fuel gas rule; the 2021 IFGC applies as a referenced code of the Ohio Mechanical Code.
OH.citation: Ohio Adm. Code 4101:2-15-01 (OMC referenced standards, IFGC-21 retained); 4101:2-1-01
OH.draft_note: Read the BBS 2024 OMC rules package: 4101:2-15-01 modifies IMC 2021 Chapter 15 and marks IBC-21, IECC-21, IPC-21, IRC-21 'Not referenced' but leaves IFGC-21 in place; 4101:2-8-01 and 915.2.2 point to the 'International Fuel Gas Code'. Inference: fuel gas is governed by the 2021 IFGC through the OMC, effective 2024-03-01. No standalone Ohio rule adopting the IFGC found. Signer should confirm against the 2025-10-15 rule text.

OK.name: Oklahoma
OK.citation: OAC 748:20-12-1 et seq. (OUBCC adoption of IFGC 2024), 43 Ok Reg No. 20; 59 O.S. 1000.23
OK.draft_note: ICC chart lag, not a conflict: ICC Apr 2026 chart shows IFGC 18 (predates the 2026-09-14 effective date). Read the OUBCC permanent rule PDF: 748:20-12-1 adopts the IFGC 2024 first printing, amended, as 'the statewide minimum code for commercial fuel gas construction', source 'Amended at 43 Ok Reg, Number 20, effective 9-14-26'. Prior: IFGC 2018, eff 2021-09-14 (38 Ok Reg 2705). OUBCC web copy is unofficial; official OAC/Ok Register text not read.

OR.name: Oregon
OR.citation: 2025 Oregon Mechanical Specialty Code, Building Codes Division (ORS 455.020)
OR.draft_note: BCD mechanical page (read): 2025 OMSC 'Based on the 2024 International Mechanical Code (IMC) and International Fuel Gas Code (IFGC)', effective 2025-10-01 with a 6-month phase-in (2022 or 2025 OMSC), mandatory 2026-04-01. Prior: 2022 OMSC (2021 IMC/IFGC). OAR division number for the OMSC not read. ICC chart lag, not a conflict: ICC shows IFGC 21, the prior OMSC base.

PA.name: Pennsylvania
PA.citation: 34 Pa. Code 403.21(a) (Uniform Construction Code, International Fuel Gas Code of 2021), 55 Pa.B. 7701
PA.draft_note: Read 34 Pa. Code 403.21(a): (3) 'International Mechanical Code of 2021', (4) 'International Fuel Gas Code of 2021', (6) 'International Plumbing Code of 2021' except that a municipality in a county of the second class (Allegheny) may not administer and enforce the IPC and keeps its Local Health Administration Law plumbing code. Section amended effective 2026-01-01, 55 Pa.B. 7701 (per IBC row; source history read). Prior: 2018 editions. Pre-2026 design contracts may use the 2018 UCC for a transition period. L&I enforces commercial work where municipalities opted out.

RI.name: Rhode Island
RI.draft_note: ICC chart lag, not a conflict: ICC Apr 2026 chart shows IFGC 18. RI SOS rule page (read): Building Code Standards Committee adopts the IFGC 2021 edition (later editions excluded), with RI amendments; current version effective 2025-12-01; prior version 2022-02-01 to 2025-12-01 adopted the 2018 IFGC (per the rulemaking description). 3-month prior-code grace to 2026-03-01 is from IBC-row search results, not read for this code.

SC.name: South Carolina
SC.citation: S.C. Code 6-9-50; LLR Building Codes Council, 2021 South Carolina Fuel Gas Code (2021 IFGC with SC modifications)
SC.draft_note: Read LLR 'Building Codes in Effect for South Carolina' PDF: Council adopted on 2021-10-06 the '2021 South Carolina Fuel Gas Code or the 2021 International Fuel Gas Code with SC modifications', mandatory for all municipalities and counties, implementation 2023-01-01. Read LLR 2024 Final Modification Index PDF: on 2025-08-26 the Council adopted the 2024 IFGC (to be known as the 2024 South Carolina Fuel Gas Code), implementation 2027-01-01. Caveat from IBC row: legislative approval of the SC modification regulations may still be pending. The May 22, 2026 State Register PDF is image-only (not read).

SD.name: South Dakota
SD.citation: None statewide; SDCL 11-10 (IBC only) and ARSD 61:15:01:01 (IBC/IFC/IMC 2015) do not adopt the IFGC
SD.draft_note: Read SDCL 34-29B-2 and ARSD 61:15:01:01 (fire marshal: IBC, IFC, IMC 2015 only) and SDCL 11-10 (IBC 2024 design standard, read for the IBC row): none names the IFGC or NFPA 54. ARSD 61:15:01:06 covers flammable liquids and LP gas (not read in full). IFGC adoption is local only (e.g. larger cities); ICC marks it X. citation_primary refers to reading the state rules that omit it.

TN.name: Tennessee
TN.scope: State minimum code via the State Fire Marshal; local governments that adopt and enforce their own codes (T.C.A. 68-120-101) may be exempt.
TN.citation: Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs. 0780-02-02-.01 (State Fire Marshal minimum codes: 2021 IFGC)
TN.draft_note: Read the SFMO 'Currently Adopted Codes' page (last updated 2025-04-17): 'The International Fuel Gas Code (IFGC), 2021 edition, published by the International Code Council (ICC)'; Code Adoption History row 4/17/2025 lists 2021 for IMC, IPC and IFGC (prior 2012, eff 2016-08-04). Same rule filing as the IBC row (01-17-25, eff 2025-04-17; 120-day option to use prior codes for SFMO plan review). No state amendments flagged for the IFGC on that page (the IBC/IFC/IPMC entries carry 'see Appendix'). Exempt local governments under T.C.A. 68-120-101 enforce their own codes; exempt list not read. Cornell/Justia copies of 0780-02-02-.01 still show the 2012 text (stale mirror).

TX.name: Texas
TX.scope: TDLR A/C licensing rule; plumbers' gas piping follows TSBPE rule (2018 IFGC via the IPC); cities adopt their own codes.
TX.citation: 16 Tex. Admin. Code 75.110 (TDLR A/C and refrigeration rules: 2024 IFGC, eff 2026-09-01)
TX.draft_note: SOURCES CONFLICT: two state rules name different editions (TDLR 16 TAC 75.110: IFGC 2024 for A/C work; plumbing board 22 TAC 367.2: 2018 through the IPC for gas piping). Read TDLR's adoption notice (2026-08-31): the Commission amended 16 TAC 75.10, 75.80, 75.110, 75.121 and 75.124 to 'update the codes adopted by reference from the 2021 editions to the 2024 editions of the International Residential Code, International Mechanical Code, International Fuel Gas Code' and the 'Uniform Mechanical Code', effective September 1, 2026. Prior text (Cornell LII, secondary): 75.110(a) 'Effective September 1, 2024, the commission adopts' 2021 IRC, IMC, IFGC and UMC; 2018 editions before. The adopted 2026 rule text itself was not read. These are the A/C and refrigeration licensing rules (Occ. Code ch. 1302); cities set their own mechanical codes (1302.303) and many use the UMC or IMC; how 75.110 applies where a city has no code was not read. No general statewide mechanical/fuel gas code. Plumbers (who do gas piping) follow TSBPE 22 TAC 367.2, which incorporates the 2018 IFGC through the IPC (2021 proposed Aug 2026). LP-gas falls under Railroad Commission rules. Two state rules carry different IFGC editions for different trades: signer should decide which one this row reports.

UT.name: Utah
UT.citation: Utah Code 15A-2-103(1)(f) (State Construction Code: 2024 IFGC), amended by Title 15A Ch. 3-4
UT.draft_note: Read 15A-2-103 version 'Effective 7/1/2026': '(f) the 2024 edition of the International Fuel Gas Code, issued by the International Code Council'; the version effective 2027-01-01 keeps 2024. Read enrolled H.B. 65 (2026 GS): '(f) the [2021] 2024 edition of the International Fuel Gas Code'; 'this bill takes effect July 1, 2026.' Prior 2021 edition (HB 532, 2023, eff 2023-07-01). ICC April 2026 chart shows 21, which predates the change (ICC chart lag). Uniform statewide code; statewide amendments in 15A Ch. 3, local amendments Ch. 4.
UT.icc_2026_10_20: IFGC 21 (ICC chart, April 2026; predates the 2026-07-01 move to 2024)

VT.name: Vermont
VT.scope: NFPA 54 National Fuel Gas Code 2021 incl. Annex G (and NFPA 58 2020), effective 2025-11-04, for public buildings.
VT.citation: 2025 Vermont Fire & Building Safety Code: IFGC references go to NFPA 54 (2021) incl. Annex G, as amended
VT.draft_note: Read the 2025 VT Fire & Building Safety Code (eff 11/04/2025), IBC 101.4 replacement: '*International Mechanical Code, shall be to the Fire Code, NFPA 1, 2021 edition, including NFPA 90A, as adopted under this Code, unless specifically adopted within these rules'; '*International Fuel Gas Code, shall be to the National Fuel Gas Code, NFPA 54 2021 edition including Annex G'. NFPA 1 2.2 adds NFPA 54 2021 incl. Annex G; Section 6 amends NFPA 54 (2021) and NFPA 58 (2020). Some IMC sections are used piecemeal (e.g. 2021 IMC 404 garage ventilation as an accepted alternative). The 2025 Plumbing Rules also replace IFGC/IMC references with the Fire & Building Safety Code incl. NFPA 31, 54, 58, 211. Applies to public buildings (20 V.S.A. 2730).

VA.name: Virginia
VA.pending: 2024 USBC cycle in progress (BHCD proposals 2026-05); no proposed/final regulation or effective date yet.
VA.citation: 13VAC5-63-10 (Virginia Construction Code, USBC Part I, Section 101.2 Note 1: 2021 IFGC as part of the USBC)
VA.draft_note: Read 13VAC5-63-10 (Section 101.2): IBC Chapters 2-35 incorporated; 'Note 1: The IBC references other International Codes and standards, including the following major codes: 2021 International Fuel Gas Code (IFGC)'; codes referenced by the IBC are part of the USBC. DHCD: 2021 USBC effective Jan. 18, 2024 (2018 USBC optional for a year). Uniform statewide; localities may not amend. 2024 cycle in progress (NOIRA 2025-03-10; proposals considered 2026-05); no proposed or final regulation found.

WA.name: Washington
WA.pending: 2024 codes (SBCC) incl. WAC 51-52: final adoption targeted 2026-10-16; SBCC says effective 2027-05-03. IFGC not named on SBCC page.
WA.scope: Natural gas per IFGC as amended in WAC 51-52; LP-gas installations per NFPA 58 (2020) and NFPA 54 (2021).
WA.citation: WAC 51-52-0101 (IMC 101.2: fuel gas regulated by the IFGC) and WAC 51-52-21101+ (WA IFGC amendments); LP-gas NFPA 54/58
WA.draft_note: Read WAC 51-52-0101 (IMC 101.2): fuel gas piping, gas-fired appliances and venting 'shall be regulated by the International Fuel Gas Code'; Exception 2: LP-gas installations per NFPA 58 (2020) and ANSI Z223.1/NFPA 54 (2021). Read WAC 51-52-21101 'Section 101 (IFGC)-General' (WA amendment of the IFGC), same WSR 23-02-055 et seq., effective 3/15/24. RCW 19.27.031(1)(b) names only the IMC (LP-gas to NFPA 58/54) and (1)(e) excludes fuel gas piping from the UPC. UNCERTAIN: no WAC sentence read that names the IFGC edition explicitly; 2021 inferred from the 2021 IMC adoption chapter that amends it. Signer: confirm the IFGC edition in WAC 51-52.

WV.citation: W. Va. Code R. 87-4-4.1.d (State Building Code: 2018 IFGC); 87-4-7 adoption by local jurisdiction
WV.draft_note: SOURCES CONFLICT (minor): City of Buckhannon Ordinance 480 (Aug 2026) says 87CSR4 changes took effect 2026-07-29 with the 2024 I-codes, but the WV SOS rule page shows the 8/1/2022 version Active and a new version 'In Progress' with no effective date (see the IBC/IRC rows). WI.name: Wisconsin
WI.scope: Commercial Building Code: public buildings and places of employment (incl. multifamily); not 1-2 family dwellings.

WI.draft_note: Read SPS 361.05: '(3) Imc. The International Mechanical Code - 2021, subject to the modifications specified in chs. SPS 361 to 366 is incorporated by reference'; '(4) Ifgc. The International Fuel Gas Code - 2021 ...'; history 'CR 23-007: am. Register August 2025 No. 836, eff. 9-1-25' (prior 2015 editions, CR 16-094 eff 2018-05-01). Transition/plan-submittal grace for CR 23-007 not checked.

WY.name: Wyoming
WY.scope: State code via fire marshal plan review for public, school, assembly, multi-story and >5,000 sq ft buildings; local codes elsewhere.
WY.citation: 041-1 Wyo. Code R. 1-2(a)(v) (Council on Fire Prevention and Electrical Safety: 2024 IFGC), W.S. 35-9-108 plan review
WY.draft_note: Read rule 041-1 Wyo. Code R. 1-2 on Cornell LII (mirror): '(iv) The International Mechanical Code, 2024 Edition'; '(v) The International Fuel Gas Code, 2024 Edition'; note 'Amended, Eff. 6/26/2024'. State Fire Marshal plan-review page (per the IBC row): 2024 International Codes adopted June 28, 2024 (2-day mismatch; rule date used). State plan review (W.S. 35-9-108) covers state/local government buildings, schools, >5,000 sq ft public buildings, multi-story, assembly; cities/counties adopt their own codes elsewhere.
